newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -MARK/YEN VOLS SLIP AS SPOT COMES OFF LOWS.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -MARK/YEN VOLS SLIP AS SPOT COMES OFF LOWS.

text.p: Implied volatilities in mark/yen options softened in Europe, with traders saying vols selling kicked in on Wednesday as spot rates recovered from 25-month lows seen earlier in the week.
In the spot market, the mark had risen a yen from its Tuesday low, which was just above the 25-month low of 62.05 it sank to on Monday.
The spot recovery soothed worries about a continued mark/yen free-fall, at least for the moment, and volatilities eased accordingly.
One-month mark/yen vols were at 11.00/40 percent at 1105 GMT against 11.50/80 in late trade on Tuesday, while one-year was quoted at 10.25/65 against 10.50/80.

"There was a lot of interest in mark/yen vols due to the fact that we were near the 62-yen level. Short-dated mark/yen vols had been holding above their dollar/mark or dollar/yen equivalents, which is very unusual," said one options trader at a German bank in London.
"But this interest in the cross should fade quickly, and dollar/mark and dollar/yen will soon take the lead again," he said.
However, market demand was still firmly biased towards mark puts, with 25-delta mark/yen risk reversals at 0.5/0.9 in favour of mark puts, unchanged from Tuesday.
Dollar volatilities were easing because the U.S. currency was settling down in ranges that were beginning to look familiar against the mark and yen after its plunge on Friday, traders said.
One-month dollar/mark vols were at 10.90/11.30 percent against late Tuesday's 10.95/11.25, while one-month dollar/yen was at 11.10/11.30 against 11.50/11.80.
Dollar/mark risk reversals were at 0.3/0.6 in favour of dollar calls against 0.2/0.5 yesterday, while in dollar/yen they were unchanged at 0.0/0.3 in favour of dollar puts.

Traders said moves in dollar vols were quiet this morning because many were sticking to the sidelines ahead of U.S. economic indicators due later in the day. U.S. July retail sales and July producer prices data are due at 1230 GMT.

"It depends on the data we get out of the U.S. today. If they are very much in line with forecasts, then we'll probably see quite a bit of selling in vols at the short end of dollar/mark, and maybe in cable and sterling/mark as well," said one trader at a British bank.
"But there certainly is room for a surprise figure, which could take spot dollar/mark further down in its correction depending on what happens in Treasuries and the Dow," he said.
Volatilities in sterling/mark were pushed higher as spot sterling was knocked down close to 2.90 marks for the first time in a month.
One-month sterling/mark vols were at 12.70/13.20 percent against late Tuesday's 11.90/12.40. Risk reversals favoured sterling puts at 0.3/0.8, the same as yesterday.
Cable vols, meanwhile, eased to 10.10/50 for one-month options from 10.30/10.60 in spite of the pound's slide against the dollar today.
Spot sterling weakened because of indications in the Bank of England's inflation report today that a pause in British monetary policy should now be possible.

Sterling/mark was pressured further because the mark gained across the board on a report by the Bundesbank, also issued today, which warned that the pace of German inflation had picked up and that the central bank would steer policy to ensure price stability.
